messages:
marie: Heads-up — customer acme-inc seeing a burst of 429s on /v1/generate since 2026-02-14 18:23 UTC. They reported a spike in latency then tails of 429s. Example request-id: req_0a1b2c3d. Tenant is tenant_acme_42, monthly plan with burst enabled. They escalated to SE and want a quick triage.

devon: Can you paste sample request headers (X-Request-Id / X-RateLimit etc) and confirm tenant id? Also any request body size or model info?

marie: Tenant: tenant_acme_42. Sample headers:
```
X-Request-Id: req_0a1b2c3d
X-Model: redwood-13b
X-Tokens-Used: 1200
Authorization: Bearer tok_... (redacted)
```
Sample curl they used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer tok_..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"prompt":"...","max_tokens":512}'
```
They say no special batching on their side.

sam: I pulled edge logs for tenant_acme_42. Spike window 2026-02-14T18:22:58 -> 18:24:10 UTC. Edge rate limiter returned reason=burst_exhausted for majority of 429s. Concurrent outstanding peaked at 120 while tenant concurrency limit configured at 100. Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/limits/limits-by-tenant (screenshot posted).

leo: Two quick hypotheses: 1) genuine workload burst > concurrency cap; 2) client-side retry amplification (replay/fingerprint) causing many near-duplicate fast retries. Check prompt hashes and request fingerprinting.

marie: How do I get per-route+model throttling attribution? I only found an overall tenant view.

devon: Run this ClickHouse snippet via infra-q to get attribution by route and model:
```
SELECT route, model, countIf(status = 429) AS throttles, uniqExact(prompt_hash) AS unique_prompts
FROM requests
WHERE tenant = 'tenant_acme_42' AND ts BETWEEN toDateTime('2026-02-14 18:20:00') AND toDateTime('2026-02-14 18:30:00')
GROUP BY route, model
ORDER BY throttles DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
I kicked it off.

observability-bot: Query job started (job id q-789). Results will be available at /play/run/q-789.

sam: Results are in. Top throttled route: /v1/generate with model=redwood-13b -> throttles=512 in that 10m window. /v1/embeddings shows 0 throttles. Also see a tight cluster of identical prompt_hash values in ~60% of requests -> indicates fingerprinting or retry loops.

marie: Customer says their client does immediate retries (no backoff) on transient latency. That could cause pileup. They also have a dashboard that polls and triggers generates.

leo: That matches amplification. Immediate mitigation options: 1) temporarily bump tenant concurrency from 100 -> 200 for 1 hour; 2) enable short smoothing in the ingress (limit bursting per-IP); 3) ask customer to add jitter/backoff. Which do we want to try?

devon: I drafted an alert rule for support to detect this earlier:
Name: tenant:burst_exhausted_v2
Expr: sum(rate(throttles{reason="burst_exhausted"}[1m])) by (tenant) > 5
For: 2m
Notify: support-oncall -> pager only if > 10 tenants affected
I'll open PR after we agree.

marie: Customer approved temporary bump. I applied the increase to 200 for tenant_acme_42 (incant: infra-admin set-tenant-limit --tenant tenant_acme_42 --concurrency 200 --ttl 3600). They reported a sharp drop in 429s within 3 minutes.

sam: Follow-up data: after bump, observed throttles drop to single digits and latency stabilizes. But we still have duplicate prompt_hash cluster — need long term fix. I'm adding a panel to the support dashboard: "throttles by tenant+model" and a heatmap for prompt_hash cardinality. PR #4320.

devon: Root cause summary: concurrent burst > configured concurrency + retry amplification (client) -> edge burst_exhausted -> 429 storm. Actions: 1) customer guidance doc with repro steps and suggested client changes (batching, jittered exponential backoff, client's idempotency keys), 2) add alert 'tenant:burst_exhausted_v2' to prod, 3) add dashboard panel and a playbook link to support runbook, 4) consider product discussion on returning 503s with graceful degradation vs 429s when model is overloaded.

leo: Filed incident INC-2026-0421 and task TCK-556 for policy discussion. :white_check_mark:

tenant-monitor-bot: Policy change request queued: ticket TCK-556. Status: queued.

marie: I'll draft the customer-facing message with timeline, repro steps and mitigation steps. Draft will include: exact times, sample req ids (req_0a1b2c3d...), snippet of the ClickHouse query we used, and recommended client code sample showing jittered backoff.

devon: Thx — please attach Grafana snapshots and the query outputs. Once customer confirms, we'll revert temp bump.

marie: Will do. Closing handoff for engineering work.
